tasks.spec:
You are a repo feature worker. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the OBE podcast repo (/mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast) at HEAD — edit files here directly.

OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY: you own exactly two paths: scripts/final_audio_check.py (new) and tests/test_final_audio_check.py (new). Nothing else. Never touch .git, never commit, never run git add; leave changes uncommitted.

CONTEXT — a near-miss on 2026-08-05: the production-publish preflight flagged retake asides ('redo that one', 'How do I do that one, AI?') in Episode 105 from a STALE INTERMEDIATE transcript (processed/transcript.txt maps to a pre-trim timeline), triggering a three-platform pause of a launch whose FINAL audio was actually clean — proven afterwards by transcribing final/episode.mp3 directly. Owner order (Ankit 2026-08-05, verbatim): 'make sure the preflight checks the final audio going forward.' Publish-blocking claims must be provable against the shipped artifact.

BUILD scripts/final_audio_check.py — a deterministic publish gate, stdlib + subprocess only, argparse CLI:
  --episode <id>            episode dir name under episodes/ (default resolution: episodes/<id>/final/episode.mp3)
  --audio <path>            explicit audio path override
  --phrases <path>          optional newline-separated extra phrases to check
  --whisper-bin <path>      transcriber binary (default /home/ankit114/.local/bin/whisper)
  --model <name>            whisper model (default tiny.en)
  --receipt <path>          receipt output (default episodes/<id>/content/final-audio-check.json)
Behavior: (1) sha256 the audio file; if a cached transcript at episodes/<id>/content/final-audio-transcript.txt exists alongside a sidecar recording the same sha256, reuse it, else run the whisper CLI (subprocess, --output_format txt) into a temp dir, store transcript + sha sidecar; (2) build the phrase list: a built-in RETAKE_MARKERS tuple — 'redo that one', 'how do i do that one', 'let me start over', 'let me redo', 'start that again', 'scratch that', 'take two', 'cut that part', 'i'll say that again' — plus any --phrases entries, all matched case-insensitively with whitespace normalized; (3) ADDITIONALLY, if episodes/<id>/processed/transcript.txt or raw/transcript.txt exists, extract every line matching a RETAKE_MARKER there and verify those exact utterances are ABSENT from the final transcript (this catches asides the built-in list misses — the intermediate transcripts are used only as a SOURCE of suspects, never as evidence of presence); (4) write a JSON receipt: {schema:'final-audio-check/v1', episode, audio_path, audio_sha256, transcriber:{bin, model}, phrases_checked:[...], suspects_from_intermediates:[...], hits:[{phrase, line}], status:'pass'|'findings', checked_at}. Exit code contract, DOCUMENTED IN THE DOCSTRING because a caller misread exactly this pattern today: 0 = pass (clean), 2 = findings (hits present — receipt says which and where), anything else = the check itself failed (missing audio, transcriber failure) and callers must treat that as UNKNOWN, never as pass. Never modify anything outside the receipt, transcript cache, and sidecar.

TESTS (tests/test_final_audio_check.py, tmp_path, stub the transcriber by injecting a fake whisper binary — a tiny shell/python script the test writes that emits a fixed transcript file): (a) clean transcript => exit 0, receipt status pass; (b) transcript containing a built-in marker => exit 2, receipt lists the hit with its line; (c) suspect harvested from a fixture processed/transcript.txt absent in final => pass, and present in final => findings; (d) missing audio file => nonzero non-2 exit and no pass receipt; (e) cache honored: second run with same sha does not invoke the transcriber (fake binary records invocation count); changed audio bytes re-invokes.

HOW TO RUN (from the worktree root — all must pass): PLACEHOLDER_MODE=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_final_audio_check.py -q -p no:cacheprovider && python3 -m py_compile scripts/final_audio_check.py

HARD RULES: stdlib only (subprocess for the transcriber), deterministic, no network, no model CLI/MCP/skills, smallest coherent implementation, leave changes uncommitted — the coordinator lands it, proves it against the real Episode 105 audio, and writes the runbook addendum.
